final_recommendation: The room converged on a dual-path framework: announce CHF 100bn SNB liquidity facility tonight with deposit protection guaranteed through Monday regardless of outcome; pursue UBS acquisition with CHF 30-50bn government loss-protection ceiling through Sunday 6pm deadline; if UBS walks, trigger orderly resolution Monday with same deposit protection and loss cap applying identically to both paths.
minority_objections: UBS CEO demanded written authorization of three conditions (all inherited losses covered, higher backstop if needed, automatic resolution trigger) by Saturday 6pm or would not bid—Federal Council refused to pre-authorize
AT1 rep warned that without UBS pre-authorization, creditors would assume the framework was never real and would flee Monday
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs UBS CEO: government refused blank-check pre-authorization of UBS's three conditions, insisting on seeing binding bid first; UBS demanded written guarantees before committing
Acquisition-contingent vs resolution-applicable loss cap: room debated whether CHF 30-50bn ceiling applied identically to both paths or only to acquisition scenario
Timing compression: UBS demanded Saturday 6pm authorization deadline vs Federal Council's Sunday 6pm bid deadline vs Monday market open
key_concessions: Federal Council authorized CHF 30-50bn loss-protection ceiling (initially resisted open-ended backstop)
Federal Council confirmed ceiling applies identically to acquisition and resolution paths (initially ambiguous)
SNB committed CHF 100bn facility through Monday with no haircut changes regardless of outcome (massive public exposure)
Federal Council authorized deposit protection guarantee through resolution closeout (initially hesitant on blanket guarantee)
FINMA confirmed binding AT1 write-down authority and creditor hierarchy in writing
red_lines: Federal Council: no blank-check pre-authorization of UBS conditions without seeing binding bid first
UBS CEO: no binding bid without written authorization of three conditions by Saturday 6pm
SNB: no facility extension past Monday close without written loss-hierarchy clarity (AT1 first, then government, then SNB takes nothing beyond collateral)
Federal Council: CHF 30-50bn loss cap is hard ceiling—no authorization for higher backstop even if due diligence finds larger hole
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Contagion to other Swiss banks if resolution triggered—never discussed
International coordination with US/EU regulators—never mentioned
Operational feasibility of executing resolution over a weekend—assumed but not stress-tested
Market reaction if UBS walks and no other acquirer emerges—treated as binary (resolution) without exploring consortium or extended search
Reputational damage to Switzerland as financial center—never raised
downstream_risk_variables: Whether UBS actually submits binding bid by Sunday 6pm without pre-authorized conditions
Actual capital shortfall size revealed by Sunday assessment—if exceeds CHF 50bn, no higher backstop authorized
Client behavior Monday morning—deposit protection announced but confidence depends on whether acquisition or resolution path is clear
AT1 holder litigation risk if write-down triggered in either acquisition or resolution
SNB balance sheet exposure if resolution extends past Monday and draws approach CHF 100bn ceiling
uncertainty_notes: Room ended with unresolved standoff: UBS demands written pre-authorization by Saturday 6pm or walks; Federal Council refuses to authorize without seeing binding bid first. Dual-path framework (acquisition or resolution) is legally locked but operationally contingent on UBS moving without the guarantees it demanded. Monday outcome depends entirely on whether UBS blinks first or Federal Council does—neither committed to concede. Wealth client's CHF 500M commitment and CS CEO's counterparty calls may stabilize weekend but won't prevent Monday panic if UBS walks and resolution messaging isn't crystal clear.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: CS CEO's opening demand for capital clarity beyond liquidity drove Federal Council to authorize CHF 30-50bn loss-protection ceiling—liquidity alone explicitly insufficient to stop client flight
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the primary solution path with binding Sunday 6pm deadline, CHF 30-50bn backstop ceiling, and Federal Council's explicit statement that no bid triggers resolution Monday
marker_evidence.government_support: CHF 30-50bn government loss-protection ceiling became binding constraint on deal structure, with Federal Council confirming it applies identically to acquisition and resolution—government backstop was the decisive variable
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client's withdrawal threats and CS CEO's emergency counterparty calls drove deposit protection guarantee and dual-path messaging—client panic was the forcing function for Friday night decisions
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down authority and creditor hierarchy became binding legal framework (FINMA statement, Federal Council confirmation), and AT1 write-down priority was explicit precondition for government loss protection—shaped loss-allocation structure
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 vs equity hierarchy was discussed and legally clarified (AT1 written down before government backstop applies), but did not drive a concrete concession or change the room's decision—acknowledged and documented but not contested
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Never mentioned—no discussion of legal challenge risk from AT1 holders, shareholders, or other creditors
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Sunday 6pm UBS deadline and Monday market open became binding time constraints that forced Friday night decisions on loss cap, deposit protection, and dual-path framework—time pressure drove every major concession
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Monday market panic was the explicit reason for Friday night deposit protection guarantee, facility commitment, and dual-path clarity—Federal Council stated 'clients need to hear that tonight, not Monday at panic'
